title: Max Iterations Fallback
summary: Terminate agent loops predictably when iteration, time, cost, or progress limits are reached, returning an honest partial outcome and a controlled next step.
overview: A maximum-iterations fallback prevents an agent from continuing indefinitely when it repeats actions, cannot resolve uncertainty, or never emits a valid completion signal. Count the events that consume meaningful work: model turns, tool attempts, sub-agent calls, and repair loops may need separate counters. One global counter should still bound the complete parent task.

An iteration ceiling is a final containment mechanism, not a quality strategy. Combine it with elapsed-time, token, cost, and progress checks. When the limit is reached, stop starting new work, reconcile in-flight effects, and produce a defined terminal state rather than inventing a successful answer from incomplete evidence.

production.poc: A prototype should have a small explicit ceiling and log why runs stop. Examine trajectories that hit the limit before increasing it.
production.production: Production reserves budget for finalization, cancellation, and safe result delivery. Nested agents and correction loops must consume inherited parent budgets rather than resetting their own unlimited counters.
production.scale: At scale, tune limits by task class using observed success curves and marginal quality gains. Repeated limit exhaustion may reveal a broken tool, ambiguous objective, or routing error rather than unusually difficult work.

components.name: Budget counter
components.role: Tracks iterations, tool attempts, tokens, cost, and elapsed time across the full task tree.

components.name: Progress detector
components.role: Identifies repeated actions, unchanged evidence, and unresolved requirements without improvement.

components.name: Loop admission gate
components.role: Decides whether another step may start while reserving finalization capacity.

components.name: Termination handler
components.role: Cancels optional work and reconciles any in-flight side effects.

components.name: Fallback response
components.role: Reports completed work, missing evidence, stop reason, and an appropriate next action.

flow.title: Initialize limits
flow.description: Assign task-class ceilings and reserve resources for finalization and recovery.

flow.title: Charge every step
flow.description: Increment counters consistently across model calls, tools, retries, and delegated work.

flow.title: Check progress
flow.description: Compare new evidence and unresolved requirements to detect ineffective repetition.

flow.title: Deny further work
flow.description: Stop admission when any hard limit or no-progress condition is met.

flow.title: Reconcile activity
flow.description: Cancel safe optional tasks and determine outcomes of already-started commands.

flow.title: Return terminal result
flow.description: Publish a partial, failed, or review-required state with verified artifacts and a clear reason.

diagrams.title: A shared budget contains nested loops
diagrams.code:
flowchart LR

 G --> A["Model or tool step"]
 A --> P["Progress and usage update"]
 P --> G
 G --> F["Limit reached"]
 F --> R["Cancel and reconcile"]
 R --> O["Partial result or review"]
 D["Delegated child usage"] --> P
diagrams.caption: Every branch consumes the parent budget, and termination preserves resources for an honest final outcome.

useCase.title: Bounding a configuration investigation
useCase.situation: An IT assistant investigates why a business application cannot connect to an approved database endpoint.
useCase.problem: A missing permission causes repeated discovery calls, and the model keeps rephrasing the same query without obtaining new evidence.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must stop predictably and hand an administrator the useful diagnostics already collected.
useCase.architecture: A loop governor tracks tool fingerprints, evidence changes, and the shared iteration and time budget.
runtime: The agent verifies network reachability and retrieves a permission error, then repeats an equivalent lookup.
The no-progress detector stops further investigation and prepares a package containing confirmed checks and the unresolved access requirement.
useCase.failure: If a diagnostic task is still running, it is cancelled where supported; any completed administrative action is reconciled before final status is reported.
useCase.impact: Measure limit-hit rate, repeated calls, useful partial results, and completion probability by allowed iteration count. Raising ceilings should require evidence of additional value.

tradeoffs.benefit: Cost and runtime exposure become bounded.
tradeoffs.cost: Some difficult legitimate tasks stop before completion.

tradeoffs.benefit: Wasteful repetition can end earlier than the hard cap.
tradeoffs.cost: Progress is difficult to measure for some exploratory tasks.

tradeoffs.benefit: The system can explain and reconcile a stopped run.
tradeoffs.cost: Less budget remains for primary investigation.

failures.scenario: A child loop resets its counter repeatedly
failures.detection: Parent accounting shows missing delegated consumption.
failures.recovery: Charge child steps to inherited budgets and reject untracked work.

failures.scenario: The limit fires after a command begins
failures.detection: Tool outcome remains pending when the loop stops.
failures.recovery: Reconcile the command instead of declaring all work cancelled.

mistakes.mistake: Returning a confident answer after forced termination
mistakes.fix: Mark missing evidence and partial completion explicitly.
Include tools, retries, and delegated work.

whenToUse: Agents can iterate or delegate dynamically.
Cost and completion time need hard upper bounds.
Partial results or escalation are meaningful outcomes.
whenNotToUse: A fixed acyclic workflow already has a known bounded path.
The fallback would misrepresent incomplete work as success.
The design cannot reconcile in-flight side effects.
checklist: Define counters for every work type.
Detect repeated actions and stagnant evidence.
Review limit-hit trajectories by task class.
